title: Norway Nutshell.

trains.name: Regular FIT
trains.blurb: The classic Norway in a Nutshell route between Oslo and Bergen — trains, the Flåm Railway and a fjord cruise, with an included Bergen fjord cruise and Mt Fløyen funicular.

transport.2: Discover Oslo on a 24-hour Hop-On-Hop-Off bus ticket.
transport.3: Norway in a Nutshell: train to Myrdal, the Flåm Railway down to Flåm, fjord cruise to Gudvangen, bus to Voss, train to Bergen.
transport.5: Bergen to Oslo by train, 2nd class.

inclusions: Norway in a Nutshell 1-day ticket, Oslo to Bergen
Bergen to Oslo train ticket, 2nd class

days.title: Arrival in Oslo
days.desc: Welcome to Norway. Make your own way to the hotel from the airport, and settle into Oslo, the vibrant capital known for its rich cultural heritage and modern urban charm. Overnight in Oslo.

days.title: Oslo
days.desc: Discover Oslo at your own pace with a 24-hour Hop-On-Hop-Off bus ticket — from the Aker Brygge waterfront to the open-air sculptures of Vigeland Park. Overnight in Oslo.
days.shopping: Aker Brygge's waterfront promenade mixes Norwegian design shops with harbourside dining — a good spot for a browse between sights.

days.title: Oslo to Bergen via Flåm
days.desc: The iconic Norway in a Nutshell route: a scenic train to Myrdal, then the Flåm Railway's descent to Flåm, one of the steepest standard-gauge railways in the world. From Flåm, cruise the fjords to Gudvangen, continue by bus to Voss, then train onward to Bergen. Overnight in Bergen.
days.experience: The Flåm Railway drops 866 metres in 20km, with a stop at Kjosfossen waterfall where the train pauses for photos beside the cascading falls.

days.title: Bergen
days.desc: A Mostraumen fjord cruise reveals dramatic landscapes close to Bergen, followed by the Mt Fløyen funicular for panoramic views over the city and surrounding fjords. Overnight in Bergen.
days.taste: Fresh seafood at Bergen's historic Fish Market on the harbour, a short walk from the colourful Bryggen wharf houses.

days.title: Bergen to Oslo
days.desc: Check out from Bergen and board the Bergen–Oslo train, one of Northern Europe's great rail journeys, crossing the Hardangervidda plateau. Spend your final evening back in Oslo. Overnight in Oslo.

days.title: Depart Oslo
days.desc: Make your way from your Oslo hotel to the airport, concluding your Norway in a Nutshell journey.

about.title: Best season
about.body: May–September for the clearest fjord views and mildest weather; the Flåm Railway and fjord cruise run year-round, but winter days are short and cold.

about.title: Weather
about.body: Coastal Norway: mild, wet summers around 15–22°C; Bergen is one of Europe's rainiest cities, so a waterproof layer is worth packing whatever the season.

about.title: Currency & docs
about.body: The Norwegian Krone (NOK) is the local currency. Norway is a Schengen Area member (though not an EU member), so no separate visa is needed for Schengen visa holders.

goodToKnow.title: Norway in a Nutshell timing
goodToKnow.body: The Oslo–Bergen leg (Day 3) is a long day combining train, rail, boat and bus connections — pack a day bag with essentials rather than digging through checked luggage between changes.

goodToKnow.title: Weather-dependent views
goodToKnow.body: Fjord and mountain views depend on clear weather — Bergen in particular is prone to cloud and rain, so treat a clear day as a bonus rather than a guarantee.

goodToKnow.title: What to pack
goodToKnow.body: A waterproof jacket is essential in Bergen regardless of season; layers for the Flåm valley, which can be notably cooler than either Oslo or the Bergen coast.

goodToKnow.title: Tipping
goodToKnow.body: Tipping is not expected in Norway — a service charge is generally built into restaurant prices, so rounding up for good service is plenty.
